The Trench Funnel primitive unifies injury availability, practice readiness, and trench efficiency into a coherent causal framework. Injury flags (DOUBTFUL/QUESTIONABLE) modulate positional snap shares through a Bayesian kernel, while practice logs refine these estimates via readiness indices. Trench efficiency metrics (RYOE) provide real-time feedback to adjust projections. The interplay creates a dynamic system where each variable acts as both input and output in a recursive feedback loop. Dualities emerge between injury severity and scheme leverage, and between practice participation and expected volume. Failure modes include over-reliance on historical proxies instead of in-season tracking, or ignoring the cumulative effect of multiple injuries on team structure. The system's robustness depends on maintaining alignment between injury reports, practice logs, and tracking data.
